newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico lawmakers say $1.3 billion is missing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico lawmakers say $1.3 billion is missing.

text.p: More than a billion dollars the government should have earned from privatization during the rule of ex-President Carlos Salinas disappeared in 1994, opposition lawmakers charged on Thursday.

"There are $1.344 billion that within the privatization process should have gone into the (government's) Contingency Fund, but since then it is not clear where they ended up," Salvador Beltran del Rio, congressman for the opposition National Action Party (PAN), told Televisa television network.
Beltran is secretary of a congressional oversight committee charged with auditing public accounts in 1994. The committee's report was sent to Congress on Thursday.

In its nightly news, pro-government Televisa reported that there was "an important gap" in funds raised from the landmark 1990 sale of state telephone monopoly Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex). Details, however, were vague.

The television network did not make clear whether the missing funds Beltran referred to were those netted in the Telmex privatization. The sale of the phone company earned the government $1.5 billion and was the largest single privatization in Mexico.
Proceeds from the privatizations were deposited in the Contingency Fund that Salinas's government set up for paying off debt and for social programs.
Shortly after he left office in December 1994, Salinas fled into voluntary exile in the midst of a lingering scandal concerning his brother Raul, who is in jail on murder and corruption charges.

Salinas's privatization program, once the toast of global investors, has already come under scrutiny amid disclosures that powerful businessmen who bought privatized firms were involved in million-dollar deals with Raul Salinas at about that time.
All the businessmen involved have denied there was any wrongdoing, but opposition congressmen have demanded an enquiry to ensure kickbacks were not involved.
